# Tools

Version 0.1.0 of the Emelia MCP server exposes **26 tools** in **4 families**. This page is generated from [`tools.json`](../tools.json), the machine-readable list of the tools as the server declares them. The server always lists every tool, whatever the family, and has no prompts or resources.

Back to the [README](../README.md).

| Family | Tools | Read | Write | Delete | Credits |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [Campaigns](#campaigns) (`campaigns`) | 7 | 5 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| [Lists and contacts](#lists-and-contacts) (`lists`) | 12 | 5 | 5 | 2 | 0 |
| [Enrichment](#enrichment) (`enrichment`) | 4 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 3 |
| [Deliverability](#deliverability) (`deliverability`) | 3 | 2 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| **Total** | **26** | **13** | **8** | **2** | **3** |

## How to read the tables

- **Read**: the tool reads your Emelia account and changes nothing (`readOnlyHint`).
- **Write**: the tool creates or changes data in your Emelia account (campaign drafts, lists, contacts, manual tasks, warmup). No tool sends an email or starts a campaign.
- **Delete**: the tool deletes data for good (`destructiveHint`). Most clients ask you before running it; keep that confirmation on.
- **Credits**: the tool spends Emelia credits. The cost is in the Notes column.
- Every tool calls the Emelia REST API with your API key and returns its JSON response. No tool declares an output schema yet.

### list_campaigns

**List campaigns**. Effect: Read. Annotations: `readOnlyHint`.

List all campaigns of the Emelia account (multichannel: email + LinkedIn steps in one campaign), with their id, name and status.

No parameters.

### get_campaign

**Get campaign details**. Effect: Read. Annotations: `readOnlyHint`.

Get the full configuration of a campaign: status, schedule, steps, and the contact lists attached to it (recipients.lists) or excluded from it (recipients.excludedLists), each with id, name and contact count. To manage the contacts of an attached list (add, update, search, delete), use the list tools with the list id.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaignId` | string | yes | Campaign ID |

### create_campaign

**Create a campaign**. Effect: Write. Annotations: none.

Create a new draft campaign with the given name. The campaign is created empty: steps, schedule and sending identities are configured in the Emelia app for now. Attach contacts by adding them to a list that the campaign uses.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | Campaign name |

> The sequence, the schedule, the senders and the lists of the campaign are set in the Emelia app: the MCP server cannot change them yet.

### get_campaign_stats

**Get campaign statistics**. Effect: Read. Annotations: `readOnlyHint`.

Get the statistics of a campaign: global metrics (sent, opens, clicks, replies, bounces...) and a breakdown per step. Optionally restrict to a date range with start/end (ISO dates).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaignId` | string | yes | Campaign ID |
| `detailed` | boolean | no | Include detailed statistics |
| `start` | string | no | Start date (ISO 8601) to filter the stats |
| `end` | string | no | End date (ISO 8601) to filter the stats |

> `end` is an exact bound: a date without a time excludes that day.

> On an unknown campaign id the error reads like an invalid API key. Check the campaign id first.

### get_campaign_activities

**Get campaign activities**. Effect: Read. Annotations: `readOnlyHint`.

Get the activity feed of a campaign (sent, opened, clicked, replied, bounced, LinkedIn events...). Replied activities include the reply content. Filter by activity type or contact.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaignId` | string | yes | Campaign ID |
| `type` | string | no | Filter by activity type (e.g. REPLIED, OPENED, SENT) |
| `contactId` | string | no | Filter by contact ID |
| `versionId` | string | no | Filter by A/B version ID |

> Returns the most recent page only (30 activities). For the full history, use the REST API or the CSV export of the campaign.

> Main `type` values: `SENT`, `OPENED`, `CLICKED`, `MAIL_REPLIED`, `BOUNCED`, `UNSUBSCRIBED`, `VISITED`, `INVITED`, `ACCEPTED`, `MESSAGE_SENT`, `INMAIL_SENT`, `LINKEDIN_REPLIED`, `WHATSAPP_REPLIED`, `TASK_COMPLETED`, `TASK_FAILED`. For replies, use `MAIL_REPLIED` or `LINKEDIN_REPLIED` (not `REPLIED`).

### list_manual_tasks

**List pending manual tasks**. Effect: Read. Annotations: `readOnlyHint`.

List the pending manual tasks of a campaign (steps that require a human action, e.g. a LinkedIn touch done by hand). Each task carries the contact, the step id (taskId) and its name.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaignId` | string | yes | Campaign ID |
| `stepId` | string | no | Filter tasks by step ID |

### complete_manual_task

**Set a manual task status**. Effect: Write. Annotations: none.

Mark a pending manual task as completed ('ok') or failed ('ko') for a contact in a campaign.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaignId` | string | yes | Campaign ID |
| `contactId` | string | yes | Contact ID |
| `taskId` | string | yes | The step ID of the manual task |
| `status` | `ok`, `ko` | yes | 'ok' = completed, 'ko' = failed |

### add_contact_to_list

**Add a contact to a list**. Effect: Write. Annotations: none.

Add a single contact to a list. If the list is used by one or several campaigns, the contact automatically enters those campaigns; this is the standard way to feed a running campaign. Flat object: field names as keys (contact fields like firstName/email/phone/linkedinUrlProfile, company fields like companyName/websiteUrl, or your custom variables; human-readable names work too). Any unrecognized key creates a new custom variable automatically. Duplicates (same email or LinkedIn URL already in the list) are not re-created: the response returns the existing leadId with duplicate: true. Set updateIfExists to true to update the existing contact instead (add-or-update).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `listId` | string | yes | List ID |
| `contact` | object | yes | The contact fields, flat key → value |
| `updateIfExists` | boolean | no | Update the existing contact when a duplicate is found |

> Contact fields are a flat object: standard fields (`firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `phone`, `linkedinUrlProfile`, `jobTitle`), company fields (`companyName`, `websiteUrl`) or your custom variables.

### add_contacts_to_list_bulk

**Add contacts in bulk**. Effect: Write. Annotations: none.

Add up to 100 contacts to a list in one call (same behavior as `add_contact_to_list` for each row: campaign propagation, duplicate detection, updateIfExists). Flat object: field names as keys (contact fields like firstName/email/phone/linkedinUrlProfile, company fields like companyName/websiteUrl, or your custom variables; human-readable names work too). Any unrecognized key creates a new custom variable automatically. Rows are processed independently; the response reports created/duplicates/updated/failed counts and a per-row result.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `listId` | string | yes | List ID |
| `contacts` | array of object, 1 to 100 items | yes | The contacts, one flat object each (max 100) |
| `updateIfExists` | boolean | no | Update existing contacts when duplicates are found |

> Loading 1,000 contacts is 10 calls of 100, not 1,000 single calls.

### update_contact

**Update a contact**. Effect: Write. Annotations: none.

Update a contact by its leadId (its list is derived automatically). Flat object: field names as keys (contact fields like firstName/email/phone/linkedinUrlProfile, company fields like companyName/websiteUrl, or your custom variables; human-readable names work too). Any unrecognized key creates a new custom variable automatically. The fields you send overwrite the contact's values; fields you don't send stay untouched. If the contact's list is used by campaigns, the updated values are propagated to them.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `contactId` | string | yes | Contact (lead) ID |
| `fields` | object | yes | The fields to update, flat key → value |

### delete_contact

**Delete a contact**. Effect: Delete. Annotations: `destructiveHint`.

Permanently delete a contact from a list (and its company data). If the list is used by campaigns, the contact is also removed from those campaigns. Cannot be undone; confirm with the user before calling it. Find the leadId with the email/linkedinUrl lookup of `get_list_contacts`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `listId` | string | yes | List ID |
| `leadId` | string | yes | Contact (lead) ID |

> Deletes the contact for good and removes it from its campaigns.

### find_contact

**Find a contact across all lists**. Effect: Read. Annotations: `readOnlyHint`.

Search a contact across ALL the lists of the account by email address or LinkedIn profile URL. Returns the lists that contain the contact and the contact data itself. Use this to answer "do we already have this person?" or to locate a contact before updating or deleting it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string | yes | Email address or LinkedIn profile URL |

## Enrichment

Family `enrichment`, 4 tools: Find a professional email or a phone number, verify an email, read a job that was still running.

| Tool | Description | Effect | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`find_email`](#find_email) | Find an email address | Credits | 1 credit, refunded when no email is found |
| [`find_phone`](#find_phone) | Find a phone number | Credits | 50 credits, refunded when no number is found |
| [`verify_email`](#verify_email) | Verify an email address | Credits | 0.25 credit, never refunded |
| [`get_enrichment_result`](#get_enrichment_result) | Get an enrichment job result | Read |  |

### find_email

**Find an email address**. Effect: Credits. Annotations: none.

Consumes credits. Find the professional email address of a person with Emelia's email finder, from their full name and company. Waits for the result (usually a few seconds). qualification is 'valid' or 'invalid'.

Cost: 1 credit, refunded when no email is found.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fullname` | string | yes | Full name of the person |
| `companyName` | string | yes | Company name |
| `companyWebsite` | string | no | Company website URL (improves accuracy) |
| `country` | string | no | Country code (e.g. FR, US) to localize the search |

> Always pass `country` (an ISO code such as `FR` or `US`): the tool marks it optional, but the search is refused without it.

> A second call starts a second search, billed again. If a job is still running, read it with `get_enrichment_result`.

### find_phone

**Find a phone number**. Effect: Credits. Annotations: none.

Consumes credits. Find the phone number of a person with Emelia's phone finder, from their LinkedIn profile URL. Waits for the result. qualification is 'found' or 'not_found'.

Cost: 50 credits, refunded when no number is found.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `linkedinUrl` | string | yes | LinkedIn profile URL of the person |

> A number already found in the last 6 months comes back at once and costs the same.

### verify_email

**Verify an email address**. Effect: Credits. Annotations: none.

Consumes credits. Verify the deliverability of an email address with Emelia's email verifier. Waits for the result. qualification is 'valid' or 'invalid'.

Cost: 0.25 credit, never refunded.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | yes | Email address to verify |

### get_enrichment_result

**Get an enrichment job result**. Effect: Read. Annotations: `readOnlyHint`.

Fetch the result of a previously started enrichment job (`find_email`, `find_phone` or `verify_email`) by its jobId. Use it when one of those tools reported the job was still running.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `find_email`, `find_phone`, `verify_email` | yes | Which enrichment started the job |
| `jobId` | string | yes | The job ID |

### list_email_providers

**List email providers**. Effect: Read. Annotations: `readOnlyHint`.

List the sending email accounts (providers) connected to Emelia, with sensitive data masked. Useful for deliverability audits: spot disconnected accounts with disconnectedOnly.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disconnectedOnly` | boolean | no | Only return disconnected providers |

### get_warmup_status

**Get warmup status**. Effect: Read. Annotations: `readOnlyHint`.

Get the warmup status of the email providers (10 per page): running or not, score, emails sent/received, spam count. A low score signals a deliverability problem.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | integer | no | Page number (10 results per page) |

> Every mailbox comes back in one call, whatever `page` you pass.

### set_warmup

**Enable or disable warmup**. Effect: Write. Annotations: none.

Enable or disable the email warmup for a provider (providerId comes from `list_email_providers` or `get_warmup_status`).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `providerId` | string | yes | Email provider ID |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | true to enable warmup, false to disable it |

> Turning the warmup off (`enabled: false`) does not work yet: turn it off in the Emelia app.

## Not covered yet

Starting or pausing a campaign, writing its sequence, choosing its senders and schedule, LinkedIn extractions and the blacklist are in the [Emelia REST API](https://docs.emelia.io/docs/all-endpoints) and in the Emelia app, not in the MCP server yet. To ask for a tool, [open a tool request](https://github.com/emelia-io/emelia-mcp/issues/new/choose).
